[BBC Business] Claude chatbot maker set for $1.3tn stock market debut despite 'catastrophic' AI warning
The AI company behind the Claude chatbot will offer its shares at between $70 and $78, which is lower than what was expected.

[BBC Business] Sales of tinned food and bottled water  jump after 'Be Ready' campaign launch
Sales of essential goods such as hand sanitiser soar after the government called on households to be prepared for emergencies.

[BBC Business] Trump says FBI investigating Nvidia boss's affair with alleged Chinese spy
The US president said he spoke with Jensen Huang on Monday and asked him about the affair with the alleged spy.

[BBC Business] US inflation higher than expected in October - here's what is happening with prices
Prices rose by 0.4% over the month, driven by increases in shelter, food and energy costs.

[CNBC] Here's the inflation breakdown for October 2026 — in one chart
The consumer price index rose 0.4% in October, a reduction from September but a level economists said is still uncomfortably high.

[CNBC] Jensen Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy further complicates Nvidia’s China problem
The allegations against Jensen Huang have brought new attention to the Nvidia CEO's potential influence over U.S. policy on chip sales to China.

[CNBC] Nvidia hires law firm Wachtell Lipton to lead Jensen Huang affair probe
On Sunday, Huang admitted to having an affair with a woman who has been connected to Chinese intelligence by reports in The New York Times and Financial Times.

[CNBC] Traders bet on a pop for Anthropic's historic IPO
Perpetual futures traders see Anthropic popping on its IPO

[MarketWatch] An overzealous Fed is quickly becoming the biggest risk to stocks in 2027
The Fed remains too sanguine on inflation, and markets too complacent, economist Neil Dutta warns.

[MarketWatch] Anthropic officially sets the stage for an IPO valuing the company north of $1 trillion
Anthropic could raise up to $63 billion in an IPO expected to take place next week.

[MarketWatch] Should a widow leave her late partner’s home to her stepkids — or cut off contact with them?
“It would be a less drastic step than selling the home now and splitting the proceeds.”

[MarketWatch] Corporate America is making a trillion-dollar mistake about retirement
The market is dramatically underpricing the economic impact of Americans age 50 and older.
